title: Chorus Scheduler for staggered stage handovers and bandwidth hedging
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Objective: Design and ship a scheduling layer ("Chorus Scheduler") that reduces token tail-latency and NCCL-induced stalls during prefill/decode handovers across tensor/pipeline-parallel stages. The scheduler uses staggered 'stage handovers' with microwindow alignment, probabilistic NCCL aggregation, and kernel-hint propagation so attention tiling and kernel selection adapt to the current cross-stage traffic pattern.

Background: We observe intermittent 95p latency spikes when a large prefill wave meets many short decode requests. Root causes include small NCCL collectives that underutilize bandwidth, mismatched kernel choices between prefill and decode (prefill favors fused prefills kernels; decode favors low-latency single-token kernels), and KV cache lease churn when stages rapidly switch roles. Existing attempts (static rendezvous windows, opportunistic coalescing) reduce some spikes but either increase average latency or hurt throughput.

Design summary: Chorus Scheduler introduces three coordinated mechanisms: 1) Microwindowed Handovers: stages accept handover windows sized to workload slack (adaptive based on per-tenant SLOs and real-time GPU utilization). Windows are staggered across pipeline/tensor ranks to avoid synchronous NCCL collectives that produce bandwidth contention. 2) Probabilistic NCCL Coalescer: instead of forcing all ranks to merge at a fixed barrier, ranks probabilistically delay non-critical collectives within the microwindow to form larger aggregations; the probability uses a short-term estimator of inter-arrival token waves to balance latency vs bandwidth. 3) Kernel Hint & Attention Tiling Propagation: the conductor attaches lightweight kernel hints and attention-tile-size suggestions to handover metadata so downstream ranks can choose kernels (e.g., fused multi-token prefill vs single-step decode) with fewer mispredictions. KV cache lease extension signals let earlier stages retain prefetched KV for a short tail beyond the handover to reduce re-prefetch churn.

Trade-offs and constraints: - Adds micro-latency for some handovers to achieve overall tail reduction; we parameterize via tenant SLO. - Probabilistic coalescing can slightly increase average latency in favor of dramatic throughput and 95p improvements when waves align. - Kernel hint protocol must remain compact to avoid added control-plane overhead; implemented as a 16-byte metadata token.

Integration and rollout: Implement as an optional scheduler mode behind a runtime flag and per-tenant policy in Dedicated/Private. Phase 1 (this ticket): implement scheduler core + kernel-hint propagation + unit tests; Phase 2: NCCL coalescer + adaptive window sizing + cluster experiments; Phase 3: rollout to canary tenants with failover to baseline conductor.

Success metrics and experiments: target 95p decode latency reduction >= 30% on mixed prefill/decode traces while keeping mean throughput within -5% of baseline. Metrics: 95p latency, mean latency, GPU utilization, NCCL bytes-per-collective, collectives/sec, KV cache hit rate. Benchmarks: use workload traces from customers A/B (internal trace IDs: trace-mix-2026-02A, trace-mix-2026-02B) and a synthetic bursty prefill/decode generator.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Chorus+Scheduler+Design, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12345, perf dashboard: https://analytics.redwood.ai/dashboards/chorus-scheduler-canary

Open questions: How conservative should the probabilistic coalescer be for enterprise tenants with strict p99 SLOs? Do we expose microwindow sizing to customers or keep auto-tuned only?
comments: 2026-03-01 - Priya Patel: Created initial RFC after investigating recurrent tail spikes on canary clusters. Attached traces and initial microwindow algorithm sketch.

2026-03-03 - Miguel Alvarez: Prototype of lightweight kernel-hint propagated via RPC metadata implemented. Local unit tests passing; kernel hint size is 12 bytes. Observed 12% reduction in kernel misprediction on synthetic traces.
2026-03-05 - Design review (K. Zhao): Request to clarify how attention tiling interacts with sparse attention models; suggested adding a safe-fallback tile mapper.

2026-03-07 - Performance triage: Early bench against trace-mix-2026-02A shows 28% improvement in 95p for decode-dominant windows and 22% improvement for mixed traces. NCCL collectives/sec down by 18%, avg bytes/collective up by 2.7x.
2026-03-09 - PM feedback (S. Kim): Prioritize exposing tenant-level policy toggles for canary rollout and add telemetry for 'collective coalescing rate'.

2026-03-10 - Action items: (1) Add safe-fallback for sparse attention as requested, (2) implement telemetry counters for coalescing decisions, (3) schedule canary rollout with one Dedicated tenant next week.
